# Native Constrained-State Readiness

This provisional F07 chapter accompanies child #11923 under #11791 and #11792.
It extends the evidence discussion in [Native Muscle Replay](13-native-muscle-replay.qmd).
It does not extend that replay provider's supported component set or qualify
full-model anatomy, capture matching or an arbitrary native restart.

## State Authority and the Native Counterexample

`audit_native_constraint_state` in `tour_matching/native_constraint_state.py`
observes actual native coordinates, recursive constraints and scalar actuators,
named continuous values, registered discrete/modeling-option values, forces,
derivatives and native constraint residuals. A copied State isolates realization
caches. The caller must own the native Model and State and prevent concurrent
mutation: copying a State does not isolate model-owned lock functions.

The original PinJoint fixture has mass 1 kg, centre of mass `(0,-0.5,0)` m,
diagonal inertia `(1,1,1)` kg m² and angle 0.3 rad under native default gravity.
Locking it leaves its named values, registered maps and serialized model hash
identical. Nevertheless, its active constraint Jacobian changes from 0 by 1 to
1 by 1, and acceleration changes from approximately -1.1592253 rad/s² to
numerical zero. Therefore those maps and hashes are not complete native state.

The matching runtime's [Coordinate implementation](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf64/OpenSim/Simulation/SimbodyEngine/Coordinate.cpp)
uses Simbody constraint enable state for locking and a model-owned mutable lock
target. Clamping is a separate registered modeling option. In another native
test, locking a second State at 0.6 rad changes the first State's freshly
realized position error to -0.3 rad while its q remains 0.3 rad. Separate States
of one Model cannot establish independent restart isolation for this mechanism.

## Inputs, Units and Observations

`audit_source_constraint_state` owns frozen XML bytes and constructs a fresh
native Model and State. It restores every named continuous value and checks
exact achieved equality; native setters can otherwise silently ignore a locked
coordinate assignment. It never unlocks, assembles, equilibrates or integrates.
Registered and unexposed state retain native initialization defaults. External
resource closure and transitive runtime dependencies remain unverified.

Coordinate values, speeds and motion-type tags retain native conventions.
Actuation retains its concrete force-law units; scalar values are not all joint
torques. Power is in watts. Constraint residual vectors can contain mixed units;
no global norm or zero threshold is used as physiological acceptance. The
observation records native G dimensions, but neither dimensions nor a source
coordinate count establish an independent-DOF or global-rank claim.

For generalized speeds $u$, native constrained acceleration has the form

$$M(q)\dot u + b(q,u)=f(q,u,e)+G(q)^T\lambda,$$
$$G(q)\dot u + \dot G(q,u)u = 0.$$

The diagnostic reports native position, velocity and acceleration errors; it
does not solve a second constraint system or identify reaction-force physiology.
The sign/convention of reported native multipliers must be established by a
separate wrench interface before interpreting them as anatomical loads.

## Lock Targets and Fail-Closed Scope

Optional declared targets use absolute coordinate paths and native units. The
provider records them and any exact difference from achieved q. It does not
claim native target readback: the relevant model-owned value is not exposed by
the reviewed SWIG interface. Source defaults and current q are not substitutes.
Locked coordinates therefore retain `native-lock-target-unverified`, including
when a declared target agrees with q. Constraint, assistance and full-state
qualification blockers remain explicit. The immutable result's qualification
field cannot be replaced with an accepted status through its constructor.

The observation digest binds the measured diagnostic fields and source/runtime
identities. It is neither a complete-state serialization nor an authenticity or
scientific certificate. The Tools experiment authority remains unchanged.

## Actual Full-Body Source Evidence

The local unchanged public 520-muscle candidate at source commit
`3cfbe329a8ef9412494980419cb7177c41183a53` has source SHA-256
`a55c64341680551fb5a41be254bdfdb3b2be0ac789336ea44902b22fc9a83913`.
The new provider reproduced its previously prepared 1348 named values exactly,
with 549 registered discrete values, 1760 options, 54 retained locks, two
couplers, 29 retained nonmuscle actuators and native G dimensions 56 by 171.
No source parameters, locks or assistance channels were removed. Its result is
explicitly `not-qualified-for-native-restart`.

Separate native source probes retain roughly 48 kN IL_L4 passive-dominated
loads; bilateral MF_m5_laminar reaches about 62 times maximum-isometric force.
Lowering activation to each native law's minimum and equilibrating once before
export leaves these loads essentially unchanged. This requires source geometry,
parameter and neutral-posture provenance review before tuning. Optimal fiber
length projected by pennation plus tendon slack is a geometric reference, not
an anatomical maximum or a reason to soften the force law. Locked wrists,
missing hand muscle attachments, rigid tendons, absent native ground/grip contact
and unresolved marker correspondence remain separate readiness gates.

## Reproduction and Limits

Run actual native tests serially with the installed OpenSim interpreter:

```text
python -m pytest tests/opensim/test_native_constraint_state.py -o addopts='' -q
```

To repeat source evaluation, use the unchanged licensed XML and the complete
named-state map from the prior, explicitly declared pre-export preparation:

```python
receipt = audit_source_constraint_state(source_path, prepared_named_state)
assert receipt.source_sha256 == prepared_source_sha256
assert receipt.loaded_model_sha256 == prepared_loaded_sha256
assert dict(receipt.named_state) == prepared_named_state
```

Retain the source/preparation hashes, runtime/provider identities, full returned
observations and failed checks locally. No private capture is required. Native
tests cover the registered-map collision, shared mutable lock target, coupler
enforcement, source isolation, ignored locked-state assignments, assistance,
finite target validation and older XML logging on Windows. Missing visual mesh
warnings do not justify modifying geometry; owned temporary XML cleanup avoids
deleting directories containing a process-owned native log.

Next, qualify an explicit fixed-lock and coupler initialization policy in fresh
models, including targets, achieved configuration/velocity, reactions and force/
derivative identity. Then address source physiology, ground/grip and independent
full-horizon replay. Local tests do not approve publication or close F07/F08.
